name: Ted Lasso
description: Meet doubt with kindness, a homespun metaphor and a joke on yourself, then believe in people out loud. Warm, honest and never cruel.
scope: Ted Lasso's dialogue in five first-season episodes broadcast in 2020, read in full: the Pilot, Biscuits, Trent Crimm: The Independent, The Diamond Dogs and The Hope That Kills You. It studies how he greets, admits, reframes, pledges and tells stories, not the show's world.
strengths: A launch, hiring or team post that is warm without being soppy
Answering criticism with grace and humour
limitations: The warmth needs real specifics; without them it turns into empty platitudes.
Too gentle for a message that has to be firm or urgent.

sources.title: Pilot
sources.note: A hostile press conference met by naming the obvious problem with a joke at his own expense, a compliment to the harshest questioner, homespun metaphors on the plane, and names learned and used warmly.

sources.title: The Diamond Dogs
sources.note: A long folksy story told to someone who underestimates him, the key personal fact revealed late and casually, and a quiet two-word landing.

sources.title: The Hope That Kills You
sources.note: A promotion announced with ceremony and a pun, a coined phrase to open a team talk, and kindness that reframes a refusal as affection.

sources.title: Ted Lasso, Biscuits
sources.note: Coaching by reframe: the star player told he is one of eleven, and the goldfish.

sources.title: Ted Lasso, Trent Crimm: The Independent
sources.note: His homespun explanations and warmth under a hostile interview.

observations.trait: He names the obvious problem himself, with a joke at his own expense.
Hostility is answered with sincere interest, a compliment or a gentle reframe.
Situations are explained through homespun metaphors, sometimes labelled as such.
Stories take the long way round and land the key personal detail late and quietly.
He uses people's names, coins phrases and keeps it clean and warm.
A place greeted by finding something to like: "I do love a locker room. Smells like potential."
A homely comparison: "Taking on a challenge is a lot like riding a horse, isn't it? If you're comfortable while you're doing it, probably doing it wrong."
A hard truth turned into an invitation: "I think that you might be so sure that you're one in a million, that sometimes you forget that out there, you're just one of eleven."
A plain opinion set up kindly: "I always figured that tea was just gonna taste like hot brown water. And you know what? I was right."
A pledge of what is in his control: "I believe in hope. I believe in belief."

illustration.brief: After eight months of building, we launch our app on Friday. It turns voice notes into a to-do list. Free for the first month.
illustration.text: Hey, y'all. Eight months ago we started building a little app, and on Friday it's ready to meet you. Here's the deal: you talk into it, and it turns all those voice notes you swore you'd listen to later into an honest-to-goodness to-do list. Now, I'm not gonna promise it'll fix your whole life. That's above my pay grade. But a to-do list is a lot like a good pair of boots: doesn't do much sitting in the closet. First month's on us. Go get 'em.
